Team — looping you in. Novatech reports p99 spikes + 5xx and throughput degradation affecting a pricing-critical path. They included logs with repeated KV cache eviction + prefetch churn messages.

Quick context: Novatech is on a dedicated pool with aggressive prefix prefetching enabled last week (config change id cfg-20280331). Anecdotally we've seen similar oscillations when hot key distributions interact with our prefetch window + dynamic eviction policy (HOL/blocking can appear when a few keys occupy the prefix cache and prefetches multiply).

Ask: can SRE/serving run an immediate triage to confirm whether this is a prefetch/configation regression vs. a model/kernel degradation? Priority: 1) stop further config rollouts to their pool, 2) temporarily tighten the prefetch window + soften eviction aggressiveness (to drop prefetch amplitude), 3) schedule a controlled canary rollback to the golden kv profile.

I'm preparing an exec-level reply to Lina and will offer a call + interim credit. Laura/Marissa please advise on low-risk rollback steps and expected RTO for a canary.

Karthik
VP, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Karthik — quick triage notes from ops:

- Observed symptom: sustained p99 latency increase (+420ms) with correlated drop in served tokens and a 5xx spike (gateway timeout / 524).
- Root symptom signals: burst of prefetch requests for ~12 high-cardinality prefixes; backend KV store shows hot set with frequent evictions. Evidence points at prefetch amplification + eviction churn causing HOL blocking on worker threads.
- Confirmed config: novatech pool is on cfg-20280331 (prefetch window=300ms, max_prefetch_keys=1000, dynamic_eviction=aggressive).

Immediate remediation plan (can be executed in parallel):
1) Freeze config rollouts to the Novatech pool (already done).
2) Deploy conservative canary to 10% of their fleet: prefetch_window -> 120ms, max_prefetch_keys -> 200, dynamic_eviction -> conservative.
3) Increase KV cache allocation to the pool by +20% (temporary).
4) Apply request-level hedging for their pricing route to avoid long head-of-line stalls.

Timing: canary config in 15min, monitor for 30min. If error/latency drops -> promote; otherwise rollback to current golden.

I'll attach the mini-runbook for the kv-playbook. Marissa — please prep an exec summary for the call and confirm credit policy baseline.

Laura
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
(attachment: runbook_kv_playbook.pdf)

- Canary will not change model weights or prompt handling; hedging is request duplication to a warm fallback worker with identical model config to avoid long tail timeouts. We will validate output parity on a small sample before wider promotion.
- We will provisionally issue a 2-hour incident credit to Novatech pending final RCA (subject to standard SLA review). Marissa will own the credit paperwork.
